captions.detailed: This 3D model is a customizable pen body featuring blocky, pixelated 8-bit style text extruded along its length. It has a long rectangular profile where the letters themselves form the outer structure, integrated with a central support beam. One end features a small cylindrical tip with a conical taper for the writing point, while the opposite end has a square profile with a circular channel running through the entire length to house a pen refill.
captions.instruction: Create a customizable, 3D-printable pen casing using a blocky 8-bit polyfont in OpenSCAD. The design should be parametric, allowing users to adjust the text string, font scale, character spacing, total pen length, outer thickness, and the inner diameter of the hole for the pen refill.
captions.factory: The script uses the 'MCAD/fonts.scad' library to retrieve 8-bit polygon coordinates for individual characters. The pen is constructed using a boolean difference operation: the union of the extruded text (via linear_extrude and polygon), a rectangular support beam (cube), and a tapered tip (cylinder and cone). Then, a square channel and a circular bore are subtracted along the length using a cube and cylinder to create the internal cavity for the pen refill.
